speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS, I need to assess the duration and characteristics of these visual symptoms. How long have you been experiencing the decreased vision and black spots, and have you noticed any floaters or flashes of light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you been adherent to your antiretroviral therapy, and do you recall your most recent CD4 count? I need to assess the severity of your immunosuppression to narrow down the potential opportunistic infections.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy
REQUEST TEST: CD4_count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages; CD4_Count: 36/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of painless vision loss, granular yellow-white opacities, and hemorrhages in a patient with a CD4 count of 36 is classic for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV retinitis
